records.name: Uttar Pradesh
records.summary:
Uttar Pradesh hosts the most trans-visible public space in India: the Kinnar Akhara (trans/hijra monastic order) fielded a Mahamandaleshwar — one of its highest-ranking monks — at the head of 15 trans spiritual leaders in ceremonial bathing at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj (Jan-Feb 2025), the world's largest religious gathering, in a collaboration with the Naga Sadhus/Aghori grouping in the making since 2015. A trans visitor at the Kumbh is inside an institutionally recognised religious hierarchy, not a marginalised underground. The inclusion is contested, however: a rival leadership instalment drew protests from within the community and other sects, gurus threatened to boycott the 2037 Kumbh, and a top-ranking trans monk who objected was physically attacked on 12 February 2025. UP also has a constituted welfare board.

Against the national 0.43, UP sits +0.03. The Kinnar Akhara inclusion is visitor-facing, seasonal, and institutionally validated by the broader Akharas' governance structures, but the festival-week attack and boycott threats show the recognition is contested rather than settled. A further counterweight exists — a single transgender woman, Kajal, was strangled in Kanpur (Aug 2025) during a robbery — but this is a lone incident with no patterned state-actor response and does not constitute a regional finding under the single-incident rule. records.name: Chhattīsgarh
records.summary:
Chhattisgarh mirrors Maharashtra's garba screening: in Bastar district, VHP and Bajrang Dal members objected to non-Hindu sponsors and participants at garba events, claiming damage to "cultural purity," and pressed religion-gated entry conditions — tilak applied to participants, Hanuman Chalisa recitation before start, and a Varaha-avatar poster circulated to organisers — with at least three garba nights called off and tickets cancelled after written objections; police received a memorandum and arranged venue security. It is the same outing mechanism as in Maharashtra, minus the Aadhaar document checks: a religion-screened gate at a public festival examines and outs gender-nonconforming visitors via actors who are not supposed to be involved. Unlike Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh has no constituted transgender welfare board (absent from the 12-state/UT list). Additionally, in November 2024 a transgender woman, Kajal (alias "Coca Cola"), was stabbed to death and dumped in an abandoned quarry in Baloda Bazar district in a Rs 12 lakh contract killing over rival claims to a community leadership seat ("guru gaddi") — a single incident with no sourced second instance, recorded for pattern awareness rather than as a decisive factor.

Against the national 0.43, Chhattisgarh sits −0.06. The combination of festival-entrance screening (visitor-facing, seasonal, outing mechanism) and the absence of any state welfare apparatus distinguishes it from Maharashtra (0.38), which carries the same screening but at least has a board. records.name: Ceara
records.summary:
Ceará is the most consistent lethal hotspot for trans and travesti people in Brazil's Northeast: 11 killings in 2024 — the region's highest toll and third nationally (G1, 28 January 2025, on the ANTRA dossier) — and 8 in 2025, tied with Minas Gerais for the highest state total of that year's 80 nationwide (Igbá Agência, 26 January 2026; SBT News). The 34% national drop is not read as improvement by ANTRA's leadership, since violence reappeared as attempted homicides (at least 75) (SBT News).

There is no state-level legal distinction: the federal constitution and penal code apply uniformly. What sets Ceará apart is sustained lethal exposure, and the national victim profile sharpens it for a visibly trans traveller — 97% of victims are travestis and trans women, over half aged 18–29, 70% of those with recorded race are Black, 97% killed in public spaces with most incidents outside capitals. Two consecutive years at the top of the ranking indicate an entrenched environment rather than a statistical blip.

records.name: Rio Granda do Norte
records.summary:
Rio Grande do Norte recorded zero trans killings in 2024 but jumped to 4 in 2025—the sharpest deterioration in the ANTRA dataset. Against a population of ~3.5 million, four cases yields approximately 1.14 killings per million per year, the highest per-capita rate among all 27 units in 2025 and roughly three times the national figure of ~0.38/million. The dossier cautions against reading a single-year zero as safety and notes the volatility.

This rate-driven exposure puts RN about 0.11 below the national 0.71. Compared with Ceará (0.61), RN's absolute count is lower (4 vs 8) but the per-capita risk is actually higher; the deviation from national is therefore slightly larger than one might expect from the raw numbers. The state sits within the Northeast bloc that accounted for 38 of 80 national killings in 2025.

No state-level statutory restriction or unique legal finding applies; the risk is purely a violence-rate signal. For a visitor, the small absolute numbers mean a single incident dramatically shifts perception, and the volatility suggests the environment can turn rapidly.

records.name: Paraiba
records.summary:
Paraíba recorded 4 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 — mid-pack in the ANTRA dossier's state ranking, alongside Paraná, Rio Grande do Norte and São Paulo — within a national total of 80 that still leads the world for the 16th consecutive year (SBT News, 26 January 2026; CNN Brasil). No Paraíba-specific statute, ordinance or enforcement policy affecting trans people was found in the audited sources; the federal framework applies uniformly.

The documented signal is therefore exposure, not law: the dossiers' consistent victim profile — young, Black, poor and Northeastern, 97% travestis and trans women, most killings in public spaces at night and outside state capitals, frequently mis-recorded by authorities — concentrates risk on people who present visibly in public. The state's absolute count doubled the best-recorded small-state figure of the same table's lower rows, and sits inside the region the dossiers identify as Brazil's hardest-hit.

records.name: Minas Gerais
records.summary:
Minas Gerais ranked 2nd nationally in 2024 with 12 killings and tied for the top in 2025 with 8 (matching Ceará). Against a population of ~21 million, the 2025 rate of ~0.38/million sits at the national average, but the consistency of appearing in the top two every year signals a structurally elevated environment compared with states that fluctuate. The 2024 total of 12 placed it behind only São Paulo.

These factors put Minas Gerais about 0.07 below the national 0.71. Compared with Ceará (0.61), which matched the same 2025 absolute count on a much smaller population, Minas Gerais' per-capita exposure is roughly half—so the deviation is more moderate. Compared with São Paulo (no deviation recorded), which led the 2024 count at 16 but fell sharply in 2025, Minas Gerais' consistency across both years is the distinguishing risk factor.

No state-specific legal restriction or unique ordinance was identified. The risk for a visitor is violence-exposure, patterned over two years, in a large interior state where the 68%-outside-capitals finding of the 2024 dossier implies added danger away from Belo Horizonte.

records.name: Pernambuco
records.summary:
Pernambuco recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, behind only the two 8-count states in the ANTRA dossier's ranking of that year's 80 national killings (SBT News, 26 January 2026; Valor Internacional). No Pernambuco-specific legal restriction or ordinance was identified in the audited sources; the federal framework applies uniformly.

The dossiers add a geographic caution that cuts against capital-centred assumptions: roughly two-thirds of such killings in Brazil happen in interior cities rather than state capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policy are weaker (SBT News). A visibly trans visitor in Pernambuco's mid-sized and interior municipalities is therefore in the geography where the recorded danger actually concentrates — alongside a victim profile of young (majority 18–29), overwhelmingly Black (70% of those recorded) travestis and trans women.

records.name: Bahia
records.summary:
Bahia recorded 7 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025 — among the highest state tallies of that year's 80, on the largest population among the upper-ranked states (SBT News, 26 January 2026; Valor Internacional). No Bahia-specific ordinance or statutory restriction was identified; federal law applies uniformly across Brazil.

The documented picture is a high absolute toll diluted by size rather than eliminated by it: the dossiers place the state inside the Northeastern region that accounts for the bulk of national killings, with the consistent victim profile (97% travestis and trans women, majority aged 18–29, 70% Black among racially identified cases, most killings outside state capitals) describing who carries the risk. For a visibly trans visitor the operative fact is persistence — Bahia appears in the top ranked band of consecutive annual dossiers — not any local legal regime.
